copies.headline: Still First, Still Scoring 99 Points
copies.body: Adam remains the best team in this league on every measure that matters: 135.8 a game, first of 12, and an 81-40 all-play that nobody else can touch. Then there's the last three weeks — 170.8, then 106.1, then 99.5, a 15-18 all-play stretch that's merely 7th of 12. Two straight losses for the defending champ and career wins leader. The roster projects for 137 a week, also first, so the talent isn't the issue; Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Bucky Irving are still Bucky Irving. Noah's next, and Noah does this in November.

copies.headline: 5-6 And Nobody Should Believe It
copies.body: Christian is 5-6 and it's a lie. The all-play says 79-42, 65%, 3rd of 12 — he's scored like a contender and banked almost none of it. Luck sits at -2.2 wins, 12th of 12, which is the statistical version of getting mugged weekly. The last three weeks: 110.4, 149.9, 133.7, with a 25-8 all-play over the stretch, 2nd of 12. That 89 draft grade was earned. CeeDee Lamb, Chase Brown, Kittle, all fine. Week 12 projects 134 against Isaac. Eventually math pays its debts.

copies.headline: John Scores Like A Contender, Wins Like A Tourist
copies.body: Second in the league at 130.5 a game, second in all-play at 80-41, and somehow sitting at 6-5 with luck at minus-1.3 — John is scoring like a two-seed and getting paid like a wild card. The ceiling is real (172.7 in Week 5), the floor is 81.7 in Week 2, which is a strange thing to put on the same résumé. The concern is forward-looking: this roster projects 116 a week, 7th of 12, and Tee Higgins can't carry a receiving corps alone. Week 12 is Logan. John's brother leads that series 6-3; this is a different problem.

copies.headline: Three Weeks Too Late, Mitchell Arrives
copies.body: Mitchell is 4-7 and playing like the best team in the league, which is the most Mitchell thing imaginable. The last three weeks: 128.6, 149.0, 162.9, an all-play of 29-4 over that stretch, 88 percent, best in the league. The problem is the 1422.9 points against, most in the league, and the minus-1.4 luck that comes with it. The roster projects 130 a week, second of 12, led by Jahmyr Gibbs and Nico Collins. CJ in Week 12 gets the version that woke up in October. Everyone else got the other one.

copies.headline: Grant Scores Like a Contender, Loses Like Everyone Else
copies.body: Five-and-six undersells Grant, and he knows it. An all-play mark of 65-56 — 5th of 12 — says he's been the fifth-best scoring team in this thing, and his 118.6 per game backs it. The luck column reads -0.9, which is the polite way of saying the schedule has been quietly mugging him. Last three weeks: 116.2, 148.5, 121.4, a 23-10 all-play stretch. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Mahomes project a combined 36 next week. Draft night graded out 80, T-9th of 12. He's outrun it anyway.

copies.headline: Fourth in Scoring, Sixth in Standings, Still Sliding
copies.body: Logan has scored 119.9 a game, 4th of 12, and gone 68-53 in all-play, also 4th — and sits 5-6 because he's taken 1399.6 points against, the 11th-fewest cushion anyone's had. Luck of -1.2 wins is real; this isn't whining. What is on him is the slide: 130.4, 117.8, 92.1, an all-play 42% over three weeks that cost him three spots. Jefferson and Burrow still project this thing at 125 a week, 4th of 12. Week 12 is John, projection 127. The dress is not fitted yet.

copies.headline: Best Roster Isaac Isn't Winning With Yet
copies.body: Isaac is 5-6 with the third-best roster projection in the league at 125 a week, which is the fantasy equivalent of owning a sports car you only drive to the mailbox. The last three weeks were real — 138.4, 130.3, 113.8, a 24-9 all-play stretch, third-best over that window — but the season average is still 111.0, eighth of twelve, dragged down by that 79.0 in Week 6. Luck is exactly 0.0, so no alibi. Ja'Marr Chase projects 26 next week. Chase and Stroud project 47 against Christian. Start converting.

copies.headline: 8-3 On Paper, 59-62 Everywhere Else
copies.body: Leif is 8-3 and nobody believes it, least of all the math. His all-play is 59-62, 49%, T-6th of 12, and he's sitting on +2.6 wins over expected, second-luckiest in the league — this is a 115.7-per-game team wearing a contender's record. The points against help: second-fewest in the league, which is not a skill. His draft night graded 80 out of 100, 12th of 12, and the roster index of 40 says the talent hasn't caught up. Josh Allen, McCaffrey and Henry project 118 against Grant. Win those, and the ledger stays quiet.

copies.headline: Six Wins, Zero Evidence, Two Straight Lucky Breaks
copies.body: CJ is 6-5 and his all-play record is 52-69 — 43%, 9th of 12. That gap isn't skill, it's the schedule handing him the 3rd-fewest points against in the league and +1.3 wins over expected. The last three weeks: 107.3, 118.3, 105.2, which is 12-21 all-play. The W2 streak is real, but so is a roster projecting 110 a week, 11th of 12. Deshaun Watson at QB and Parker Washington as the top projected receiver is not a plan. Week 12 says 117 against Mitchell.

copies.headline: 7-4 Built Entirely Out Of Scheduling Luck
copies.body: Kaleb is 7-4 and nobody is buying it. He averages 103.7 a game, 12th of 12, and his all-play is 45-76 — a 37% win rate dressed up as a contender. The +2.9 luck figure is the luckiest in the league, and the 1,133.4 points against is the fewest anyone has faced. The last three weeks: 76.8, 127.4, 108.7. That 86 draft grade tied for 4th of 12, which makes the 107 weekly projection — 12th of 12 — genuinely impressive mismanagement. Peter's up Week 12.

copies.headline: Best Draft In The League, Worst Month
copies.body: Peter won draft night — 89 out of 100, first of twelve — and has spent the eleven weeks since turning that into 107.0 points a game, 10th of 12. The L4 streak is bleak: 93.9, 118.0, then a season-low 66.3, an all-play of 5-28 over three weeks. He's 5-6 only because luck has handed him +0.9 wins he didn't earn, and 45-76 all-play says the real team is worse than the standings. Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers deserve better. The 2022 champ is projecting 111 against Kaleb.

copies.headline: The Assassin Is Out Of Bullets
copies.body: Noah's whole brand is the postseason — five career playoff wins, three Cinderella runs' worth of nerve — but you have to make the field first, and 3-8 with a 38-83 all-play isn't a slow start, it's eleven weeks of evidence. The last three games: 109.4, 91.4, 89.2, a 5-28 all-play stretch. That draft scored 86, T-4th in the league, which makes this worse, not better. Jayden Daniels and Garrett Wilson are fine. The lineup around them projects 112 a week, 10th of 12. Adam's next. Pack the dress.

intro: Adam holds the top spot at 66.9 and he's earned it the boring way: 135.8 a game, a 67% all-play mark that leads the league, and a minus-0.4 luck rating that says the 7-4 record is real. Noah sits at the bottom with a 31.2, which is what happens when you score 104.6 a game, win 31% of your all-play matchups, and post a 15% form number with a luck rating of minus-0.5 — nobody robbed him, he just hasn't been good. The week's loudest move is Mitchell, up from seventh to fourth on an 88% form rating that's the best on the board, though it's worth noting he's still 4-7 with a 49% all-play, so the engine likes the last month more than the season. Leif is 8-3 and ranked eighth, which should tell you everything about a plus-2.6 luck score.
